pranav_sre: Seeing a bump of transient gRPC errors between gpu-node-pool nodes, started ~10:23 UTC. Symptoms look like packet loss on the overlay (Geneve) only during heavy KV cache churn.

maria_neteng: Which nodes are hit? same rack/az? any NIC commonality?

pranav_sre: Mostly east-west within az-3 (gpu-pool-a). All affected hosts show Mellanox ConnectX-5 (mlx5) and kernel 5.15.x. Not seeing it in gpu-pool-b (intel igb, kernel 5.10).

kevin_infra: Any pcap/tcpdump? can you reproduce with iperf?

pranav_sre: Ran short iperf3 run between two pods on same node (host-network -> pod) and cross-node. Cross-node shows periodic 200-500ms pauses and ~1-2% retransmits. Local node traffic is fine. tcpdump on host reveals bursts of small packets + retransmits at the same times. Snippet:```
12:34:56.789012 IP 10.0.12.5.42324 > 10.0.14.7.8777: Flags [P.], seq 12345:13705, win 29200, length 1360
12:34:56.789045 IP 10.0.12.5.42324 > 10.0.14.7.8777: Flags [.], ack 13705, win 30000, length 0
12:34:56.789312 IP 10.0.12.5.42324 > 10.0.14.7.8777: Flags [P.], seq 13705:15065, win 29200, length 1360
...
12:34:57.000000 IP 10.0.12.5 > 10.0.14.7: ICMP 10.0.14.7 unreachable?
```

sara_oncall: ICMP unreachable in tcpdump often points to mtu or fragmentation issues on overlay. What MTU on host and geneve interface?

pranav_sre: Host eth mtu=9000, kube-bridge/geneve device mtu=1450 (we set that when enabling jumbo for host). But I noticed some hosts still report eth0 mtu 1500 after kernel reboots (we had mixed config). Could be mtu mismatch.

maria_neteng: That's suspicious. Geneve adds ~38 bytes overhead (outer hdr + geneve). With eth mtu 1500, inner payload 1500 -> outer will fragment/drop. With offloads it can be worse. But with Mellanox + GSO/GRO, there's a known interaction where segmented SKBs with large GSO/TSO and Geneve header cause vnet path to drop/skipped skb linearization on certain kernel versions.

kevin_infra: Can you try disabling GSO/GRO/TCP segmentation offloads on one affected host as a quick test? If it clears, we can roll a node-level workaround. CPU cost will go up but helps confirm.

pranav_sre: Did that on one node:```
# ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
# ethtool -K geneve0 gro off gso off tso off
```
After that, iperf3 shows steady throughput and retransmits drop to ~0.1%, gRPC timeouts disappeared for the test window. So disabling offloads reduces drops.

deploy-bot: Deploy job 2134 started: rolling ethtool workaround to 1 node in gpu-pool-a for canary.

maria_neteng: Good repro. Short-term mitigation: we can push an init script for gpu-pool to disable GSO/GRO on geneve interface (and eth0) for nodes with mlx5 + kernel 5.15. Medium-term: there was a kernel fix for vxlan/geneve GSO handling in 5.19+ (skb linearization/GSO split bug). We should plan kernel upgrade or backport patch for the affected release.

kevin_infra: Also verify NIC driver firmware (mlx5_core). Older fw + offload combos are more fragile. Can ops try updating firmware on a single canary host as a comparison?

pranav_sre: Will do fw bump on canary after the ethtool canary. Also found a workaround where adjusting overlay mtu to reserve gso overhead helped a bit: geneve mtu 1450 vs host 9000 mismatch was fixed by forcing host eth mtu to 8962? but that's messy.

sara_oncall: Action items: 1) prio: roll ethtool workaround to rest of gpu-pool-a nodes (canary -> 20% -> 100%) until kernel fix available. 2) schedule mlx5 fw upgrade canary and compare. 3) plan kernel upgrade across pool or backport patch. 4) add monitoring alert for geneve retransmit rate > 0.5% to detect recurrence.

maria_neteng: I'll open a runbook snippet for the ethtool workaround + commands and CPU impact note. Also add note about verifying host mtu consistency (host eth mtu must be >= overlay mtu + geneve overhead).

pranav_sre: Thanks — rolling now. Will post results in this thread once canary completes (~20m).
